clue.text: Tory party primarily mock member protection

parts.note: CON is the short form of Conservative, the Tory party
a do is an informal party

indicators.note: primarily means in the first place, so only the opening letter of the following word is wanted

parts.note: first letter of mock

explanation.surface: A Conservative party conference staging a mocking attack on a protective MP.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads like political satire about shielding an MP; 'member' is the cheeky slang sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheath worn over the penis, the bodily member, as a barrier against pregnancy and infection.

clue.text: Wealth? Put a limit on the lot abruptly!

indicators.note: something ended abruptly is cut short, so the phrase loses its final letter

parts.words: Put a limit on the lot
parts.note: to cap it all is to put a limit on everything

explanation.surface: An exasperated call for a ceiling on wealth, cut off mid-sentence.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase 'cap it all' run together and docked of its last letter gives CAPITAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Capital is accumulated money and assets, the stock of riches an owner holds.

clue.text: Revolutionary left with a smack on the buttocks

indicators.note: a revolution turns things round, so the assembled letters are read backwards

parts.note: L is the standard abbreviation for left
taken as written
to tan someone's hide is to give them a beating

explanation.surface: A left-wing revolutionary gets a spanking.
explanation.walkthrough: NATAL here is not the birth word but the rarer anatomical adjective from Latin nates, the buttocks.
explanation.definitionFit: The anatomical adjective natal refers to the nates, the rump, so it describes things located at the rear seat.

clue.text: Compulsive bosses I've sent crazy

indicators.note: letters driven crazy are thrown into disorder and rearranged

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A compulsive habit that the speaker's managers find maddening.
explanation.definitionFit: An obsessive person acts from compulsion, driven by fixations they cannot resist.

clue.text: Gas associated with large behind? It could lift you off your feet!

definitions.text: It could lift you off your feet

parts.note: wind is intestinal gas
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large
ass is slang for the backside

explanation.surface: A lavatorial joke: a big bottom's flatulence powerful enough to launch you.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on the fart joke; a windlass is a winch, which really can hoist a person.
explanation.definitionFit: A windlass is a winch with a horizontal drum turned by a crank, used for hoisting heavy loads such as anchors.

clue.text: Hoskins is who I am! One ghastly twerp essentially without limits!

parts.note: the setter speaking of himself: I am, shortened
the speaker's own pronoun

indicators.note: the essence of a word is its core, so the central letter of each of the three words is taken

parts.note: the central letter of a three-letter word
the fourth of seven letters
the third of five letters

explanation.surface: The setter boasting, then calling himself a dreadful idiot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without limits' looks like an instruction to remove outer letters, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something immense is so vast it seems boundless, too great to be measured.

clue.text: Drug-taker embarrassed about securing work

indicators.note: to secure something is to hold it firmly inside, so one piece goes within the other
about can mean turned around, so the word for embarrassed is read backwards

parts.note: embarrassed people go red in the face
OP is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: An athlete caught doping is red-faced about holding on to a job.
explanation.definitionFit: A doper is someone who takes illicit drugs, especially a cheating athlete.

clue.text: A couple of lines on a table? Time to get on it, folks!

definitions.text: Time to get on it, folks!

parts.note: taken as written
L is an abbreviation for line; a couple gives two
taken as written
a board is a table, as in bed and board

explanation.surface: Two lines of cocaine on a table, and an invitation to partake.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests drug-taking; the definition is the conductor's call before a train departs.
explanation.definitionFit: The guard's traditional shout tells passengers to board the train or boat before it leaves.

clue.text: Genuine as Russian leader? That's nonsense ultimately!

parts.note: as and since both mean because

indicators.note: the leader is the one at the front, so the initial letter of Russian is used

parts.note: first letter of Russian

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the final letter is taken

parts.note: last letter of nonsense

explanation.surface: Someone questions whether a Russian leader could be honest, and dismisses the idea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Russian leader' suggests TSAR or PUTIN, but it only means the letter R.
explanation.definitionFit: Sincere means honestly felt, free from pretence or deceit.

clue.text: Unsuccessful incarceration judge covered-up

indicators.note: something covered up is hidden from view, so that letter disappears

parts.note: jailing is putting someone in prison
J is the abbreviation for judge

explanation.surface: A judge hushes up a failed attempt to imprison someone.
explanation.definitionFit: An ailing firm or campaign is in poor health, struggling and failing to thrive.

clue.text: I am so put out about Special K

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the rearranged letters go around the extra one
put out suggests disturbed, so these letters are knocked into a new order

parts.note: taken as written for the rearrangement
doubles as part of the letters to rearrange
S is the abbreviation for special

explanation.surface: Someone is annoyed about Special K breakfast cereal.
explanation.walkthrough: Special K is a breakfast cereal brand; here K is the chemical symbol, and 'put' does double duty as fodder and indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: K is the chemical symbol for this soft alkali metal, from its Latin name kalium.

clue.text: Comic actor student's seen in drag

indicators.note: to be seen in something is to be inside it, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: a drag and a pain are both bores or nuisances
L for learner, read as student is

explanation.surface: A comedian who also studies is spotted wearing women's clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: Michael Palin of Monty Python often appeared in drag, which suits the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Michael Palin is a British comedian and actor, a member of the Monty Python team.

clue.text: Pork pies can come with Tango and beers

parts.note: T is Tango in the NATO phonetic alphabet
ales are beers

explanation.surface: A pub snack of pork pies served with a fizzy drink and beers.
explanation.walkthrough: Tango is a British orange soft drink; 'pork pies' is Cockney rhyming slang for lies.
explanation.definitionFit: Tales are fibs or untruths, and pork pies rhymes with lies in Cockney slang.

clue.text: Artist that base nurses easily brushed aside

indicators.note: to nurse is to hold close and cradle, so one piece is held inside the other

parts.note: base and ignoble both mean low and dishonourable
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A painter's low-grade work is dismissed without a thought.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ignorable can safely be disregarded, so it is dismissed with little effort.

clue.text: Needing support, Bolshevik leader turns to Left

indicators.note: turns to means becomes, so one letter is swapped for another

parts.note: backing is support

indicators.note: the leader comes first, so the opening letter of Bolshevik is used

parts.note: first letter of Bolshevik
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A Bolshevik leader in need of support defects to the political Left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bolshevik leader' points to Lenin, but here it is just the letter B.
explanation.definitionFit: If you are lacking something you are without it and therefore in want of it.

clue.text: Plant in bud rocketed skywards

parts.note: bud means mate; Cockney rhyming slang china plate also means mate
something that rocketed skywards went up

explanation.surface: A plant's flower bud shoots up rapidly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bud' looks horticultural but means a pal; in Cockney rhyming slang a mate is a china, from china plate.
explanation.definitionFit: The China rose is a shrub of the rose family native to China, also a name for a hibiscus.

clue.text: European worried about soldier's discharge

definitions.note: read as a verb, to give off

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the first pair of words goes around the next

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for European
a man is a soldier in the ranks
something that ate at you worried you

explanation.surface: A European fretting over a soldier's dismissal from the army.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Discharge' suggests leaving the army, but it is the verb meaning to send out.
explanation.definitionFit: To emanate is to flow or issue from a source, as a smell or light is given off.

clue.text: Wild and naughty and on a bed?

indicators.note: lying on a bed puts something within its bounds, so the pair goes inside

parts.note: taken as written
the word itself
the word itself, doubling as the placement signal

explanation.surface: A saucy question about frolicking in bed.
explanation.walkthrough: The little word 'on' serves twice, as its own letters and as the signal for placing them inside the bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Abandoned behaviour is uninhibited and unrestrained, freed from propriety.

clue.text: Weapon offensively loud son pulled out

indicators.note: something pulled out is withdrawn, so that letter is removed

parts.note: strident means harsh and grating
S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A noisy son is withdrawn from something, perhaps an armed conflict.
explanation.walkthrough: Trident is also the name of Britain's nuclear missile system, apt for 'weapon'.
explanation.definitionFit: A trident is a three-pronged spear, as carried by Neptune, and a British nuclear missile.

clue.text: Jazz fan upset with bluesman changing direction

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, and in a down clue that turns the word upside down

parts.note: cat is jazz slang for a fan or musician
B.B. King was a celebrated blues guitarist

explanation.surface: A jazz lover is annoyed with a blues player who switches style.
explanation.definitionFit: Tacking is the sailing manoeuvre of turning a boat's bow through the wind to alter course.

clue.text: Cream-covered bun or tart

indicators.note: something covered has a layer over it, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: the cream of anything is the top
a bun is a bread roll

explanation.surface: A choice at the bakery between a cream bun and a pastry tart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tart' looks like a pastry beside the bun, but it is the insulting slang sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are dated insults for a woman regarded as promiscuous or slovenly.

clue.text: One taking the piss out of British hierarchy?

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for British
a ladder is a hierarchy of ranks, as in the career ladder

explanation.surface: Someone mocking the British class system.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taking the piss' is British slang for mocking someone; read literally, the bladder holds urine.
explanation.definitionFit: The bladder is the organ that collects urine, literally taking it in, a joke on the slang for mockery.

clue.text: Does stupendously well to steal small bust

definitions.note: singular noun defining a plural answer

indicators.note: stealing takes something in, so one piece is taken inside the other

parts.note: a business that booms is thriving
S is the abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: A thriving operation pinches a tiny statue of someone's head and shoulders.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's bust is her breasts, informally called her bosoms.

clue.text: Her Maj takes a tumble over frock to get compensation!

indicators.note: tumbling turns something head over heels, so the title is flipped

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen
a frock is a dress

explanation.surface: The Queen trips over her gown and wants damages.
explanation.walkthrough: Her Maj is a jokey British name for Her Majesty the Queen.
explanation.definitionFit: Redress is reparation paid to set right a wrong or grievance.

clue.text: Curl up with a soup, being the worse for wear

indicators.note: up can mean in a state of commotion, so the surrounding letters are stirred into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone hungover curls up on the sofa with a bowl of soup.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Curl up' reads as one phrase, but 'up' is detached to signal the mix and is not part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Crapulous means suffering the effects of heavy drinking, sick from excess.

clue.text: Female in brigade failing physical education?

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: a brigade is a military unit
F is the abbreviation for female

explanation.surface: A woman in an army brigade flunks the fitness test.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is playful: someone failing a PE class may simply be out of shape.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone not in good physical shape could be expected to do badly in a gym class.

clue.text: Consumed drop of daiquiri after daughter went out

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for daughter
consumed food is eaten

indicators.note: a drop is just a tiny amount, so only the first letter is used

parts.note: first letter of daiquiri

explanation.surface: Someone had a sip of cocktail once the daughter had left the house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Went out' looks like left, but it is the courting sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Two people who dated went out together romantically.

clue.text: Undecided about husband being a source of irritation

indicators.note: about means around, so the first word wraps round the next

parts.note: torn between options means undecided
H is the abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: A wife unsure about her husband, who annoys her.
explanation.definitionFit: A thorn in one's side is a persistent annoyance or nuisance.

clue.text: Shot during curtain of fire

indicators.note: during means within the span of, so the answer lies inside the following words

parts.note: letters running across the words

explanation.surface: A shot fired amid a barrage of gunfire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shot' suggests gunfire, but it is a billiards term.
explanation.definitionFit: In billiards or snooker, an in-off is a stroke where the cue ball enters a pocket after striking another ball.

clue.text: Someone swimming around lake east of Luxembourg could be a swimmer

indicators.note: in an across clue, east of means placed to the right, so the rest follows

parts.note: L is the international vehicle code for Luxembourg

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the rearranged letters enclose another
swimming suggests things floating about loosely, so the letters drift into a new order

parts.note: letters to rearrange
L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: A person swims in a lake east of Luxembourg.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swimmer' sounds like a person, but it is a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The lemon sole is a flatfish of European seas, a swimming creature as an example.

clue.text: Pet with rage wrestling with a chimpanzee?

indicators.note: wrestlers grapple and tumble, so these letters are twisted into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A furious pet grapples with a chimp.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the chimpanzee as one example of the category.
explanation.definitionFit: Chimpanzees belong to the hominid family alongside gorillas and orangutans, the large tailless primates.

clue.text: Like to cuddle academic that's one hot dude!

indicators.note: a cuddle wraps arms around someone, so one piece holds the others inside

parts.note: as means like
a don is a university teacher
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone longs to cuddle a lecturer they find very attractive.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Adonis was a beautiful youth loved by Aphrodite, so the name means a handsome man.
